#4162. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4161. The First Review For Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Is In

Update [Wed 4th Nov 2026, 11am]: And would you believe it, you can now check out the Nintendo Life verdict in our own review:

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

Original Story: It's a huge week in gaming with the highly anticipated launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2. The first review from the famous Japanese outlet Famitsu has now officially gone live. So, what did it think of Nintendo's remake?

If you aren't familiar with this publication's unique scoring system, four critics each deliver a score out of ten, and these scores are then totalled. For Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2, it's received 9/9/9/10, giving it an overall score of 37/40. So, it's been well received by the outlet!

In case you need a reminder, the original 1998 Nintendo 64 game was awarded a "perfect" score of 40/40. As for the 2011 3DS release, it was also given a score of 37/40. We'll be delivering our own final thoughts here on Nintendo Life later today, and be on the lookout for a review round up.

What's your reaction to this review score from Famitsu? Are you jumping into the remake this week? Tell us in the comments.

#4160. Sony Seemingly Winding Down PSVR2 Sales, Gone from USA Store

Sony may be taking steps to wind down sales of its PSVR2 headset, as it's been spotted that the VR device is no longer being sold through some of its official regional outlets and at third-party retailers.

For a few weeks now, fans have been picking up on the fact PSVR2 no longer appears on the official PlayStation Direct website in the USA. I did a search of the website today, and the headset is nowhere to be seen.

If you scroll down the PS5 accessories tab on the USA webpage, you'll find a PSVR2 heading, but the actual device isn't there. You only receive options to purchase the charging station, the PC adapter, and a third-party case:

Besides these examples within the PSVR2 tab, I can find absolutely no evidence the VR device exists on the PlayStation Direct site for USA customers. For now, at least, the PSVR2 headset is still for sale on the UK side of PlayStation Direct.

The situation goes further, though, according to Road to VR, which has done a deep dive into regional data relating to PSVR2. According to them, the removal of the headset from regional PlayStation Direct pages began in mid-October, which is when fans started noticing it was gone. The link that should have taken you to the PSVR2 purchase page was producing a 404 error.

As the outlet also highlights, retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart do have stock listed, but it comes from third-party retailers at considerable markups over the normal price of the headset — around $750 at Best Buy.

It appears more difficult than ever to buy a PSVR2 at its recommended retail price.

News Sony Seemingly Ends VR Ambitions by Selling Patents to Meta

To get a better gauge on what's happening, it'll be interesting to see if any PSVR2 discounts are revealed around Black Friday. Last year, Sony knocked $100 off the price for the spending period. It'll be interesting to see if anything happens this month — and if there's even stock to facilitate a discount.

Of course, PlayStation's first-party support for PSVR2 has been woeful. Third-parties have brought their games to the VR platform, but Sony called it a day on launch, after Horizon Call of the Mountain, in terms of dedicated PSVR2 titles. Most recently, it sold its VR patents to Meta, which hammered another nail into any VR efforts from Sony in the future.

Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.

I bought a PSVR2 at launch and while I was mildly surprised by Sony’s post Horizon lack of support (outside of Gran Turismo) I was and remain happy with my purchase because it got quite a few great games.

Below is a post I wrote on the subject earlier this year. I stand by the premise (that niche and dead are different things) though I concede that I was a bit too optimistic about the PSVR2.

It was always clear sales were low but I had thought Sony was selling it at cost or a profit (usually the case for peripherals as opposed to consoles). If they are dropping it they were probably selling it for a loss.

VR will always be niche but I suspect someday it will be a profitable niche for a clever company who releases something at the low end that needs relatively few sales to be profitable (think the VR equivalent of the Nex Playground). Not this gen though and Sony clearly won’t have anything to do with it.

https://www.pushsquare.com/features/video-silence-as-psvr2-turns-three-years-old-is-sonys-ps5-headset-dead

Niche and dead are different things. VR is dedicated hardware which blinds and deafens the user to the outside world so it’s sales are going to be fraction of that of more open dedicated hardware like consoles and portables whose sales are of course a fraction of generalist hardware like cellphones and PCs.Along those lines VR games are niche. If you spend vast amounts of money on them or slap an expensive license (such as Marvel) on a VR only game, some will applaud you, but that won’t grow your audience, it just means you lose more money. Spending the big money some claim they are waiting to see spent clearly doesn’t mean anything since Meta burned tens of billions on VR without growing the market.

I would have liked to see Sony fund a VR studio or three though as a guy who happily plays good games regardless of their publisher I wasn’t too put out.

Setting aside the continued strong VR support of the ever growing GT7 and No Man’s Sky, PSVR2 has had a steady stream of quality games. Recentish examples that spring to mind are Roboquest VR (which has been dominating my VR playtime in recent weeks), Demeo x DnD: Battlemarked, VRacer Hoverbike, Ghost Town, Lumines Arise and Aces of Thunder. Of course if past games like Humanity, Synapse, Pistol Whip, RE4, Arken Age, Hubris, Rez Infinite, Moss Book 2, Arizona Sunshine 2, Before Your Eyes, Ironguard and Max Mustard didn’t turn people’s heads it’s logical the current and upcoming slate isn’t going to either so I don’t expect sales to radically improve anytime soon, though the recent (temporary?) price cut to $300 will certainly help sales a bit.

So no, PSVR2 in particular and VR in general aren’t dead, but they are niche so budgets and expectations have to be set accordingly (I think realistic big budget games are either going to be flat to VR ports or games than run on both). Speaking of setting, one can set your watch to yearly articles declaring the niche dead because it’s a niche inbetween articles bemoaning the industry’s obsession with growth and profit maximization 😋.

@lacerz @Northern_munkey Look, i don't want to get in a back and forth. Just want to say, yes, i have tried, which is why i know what i said. I got games for it and could not do it. It was the motion sickness and the unconfortable experience as well as the eyesight strain (i call it crossed eyes). It's just not a pleasent experience.

Now, of course this doesn't invalidate your experiences. You enjoyed it and that's fine. There are some genres that are suited for it. But, for general gaming, it's not there.

@WaveWitch I agree in part. VR hasn't taken off as a mainstream proposition, and I can see why. It's not just form factor or technical specs. It's friction, comfort but, mostly, the abstraction model.

Sitting on a couch in front of a TV while controlling a character on screen is a tried-and-true abstraction model that just works. VR is awesome, but it raises a number of abstraction issues that haven't been fully addressed yet. You're supposed to embody the game character but, to this day, it feels janky and disconnected. And motion sickness is a symptom of that. "Grow your VR legs" is not something most people are willing to do.

Driving in VR with a racing rig is the closest one can get to that 1-to-1 abstraction promise. Add a motion simulator, and you might get to the wholly grail. But again, not mainstream at all.

I'm not saying VR is dead. VR gaming is dead as a mainstream proposition, but VR will live on in many ways: in gaming, as a niche market; in corporations, as an invaluable tool in certain scenarios; and, maybe, as a primary way to interact with digital content, as Meta VR Glasses seem to bet on. I still believe in that use case, but it's impossible to predict when it will catch on.

#4159. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.

#4158. Former Xbox COO Issues Lengthy Departure Statement To 'Set The Record Straight'

"This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end."

This time last week, we mentioned how newly-promoted Xbox Chief Operating Officer Helen Chiang was suddenly leaving Microsoft after 21 years, with a suggestion at the time that she may have been "terminated for policy violations".

Chiang has now taken to LinkedIn to share a lengthy departure statement in which she denies she was fired for a policy violation, but nevertheless suggests concerns regarding how certain things were handled in her case.

The statement does the talking for itself, so we'll share it in full down below:

"Clarity is Kindness There has been some speculation about my abrupt departure from Microsoft, including claims that I was “fired for a policy violation”. That’s not accurate and while I won’t turn this into a play-by-play, silence should not be mistaken for agreement. What has been said about my departure, and what has been left unsaid, has created a picture of me that I hardly recognize. It’s important to me to set the record straight. First, I did not leak confidential company information to the press. I have never communicated with any journalist outside the limited, company-authorized interviews I’ve done as part of my job. That includes every journalist who reached out this week seeking my side of the story. Second, I did not leave XBOX to join a competitor. You don’t spend two decades somewhere without developing a deep loyalty to the people, teams, and businesses you’ve helped build. XBOX was never just another stop in my career. My end game was always to keep building here. Third, I did not engage in discrimination, bullying, harassment, insider trading, embezzlement, or other fraudulent activity. I stand by my record: both the results I delivered and the way I have treated people throughout my career. I won’t let speculation define my character or erase that record. Lastly, I did not leave because I was passed over for a bigger role. Since having children, I’ve been intentional about how I define ambition and success. I haven’t actively sought out bigger roles or increased responsibilities, and the last time I interviewed for a job was in 2011. My reputation and results paved the way for the opportunities that followed. I went where the company believed I was needed and where I could have the greatest impact. I did not ask for my most recent role, either. I was promoted into it in July. I believe in fairness, accountability, and holding ourselves to the standards we expect of others. Those standards only mean something when they’re applied consistently. I have serious concerns about how they were applied in my case, and I believe those concerns deserve to be taken seriously. I share this because I don’t want my departure reduced to an inaccurate story about incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal. My story is about staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard. That’s the legacy I hope to leave behind. To everyone who has reached out with hugs, love, and support: thank you. So many of you have reminded me of the wonderful times we’ve shared over the past 20 years and the impact we’ve had on one another. Some of you I haven’t been in touch with for several years, yet you still took the time to check on me. Others are people I’ve never even met, but you reached out anyway. That speaks volumes about the care and humanity in our industry and the connections that transcend where we work. This is not how I ever imagined my story here would end. And it is not the whole story."

As you can see, Chiang starts her statement here with the phrase "clarity is kindness", which is a phrase that Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has used on numerous occasions since taking her role a few months ago.

Nothing specific is said about why Chiang was let go (or potentially decided to leave) as part of this statement though, and while she's certainly assertive in getting her point across, there's no evident malice directed at anyone.

Ultimately, she says she's publishing this statement to avoid being linked to "incompetence, ambition for the next big job, or a Nelson-level scandal", and that her story is about "staying true to your core values, especially when it is hard".

On behalf of everyone at Pure Xbox, we wish Chiang all the best in her future endeavours.

News Xbox's Newly-Announced COO Is Leaving Microsoft After 21 Years

"I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well"

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

#4157. All the hype has already made Crimson Desert one of the biggest launches on Steam this year

We're merely days away from the end of the first quarter of 2026, and Crimson Desert has come in clutch to join the list of big sellers.

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

This peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#4156. Crimson Desert's first patch aims at fixing controls, but it mostly affects mouse and keyboard

The first post-launch patch for Crimson Desert is here, and the list of changes is promising, even if it doesn't go far enough to address some deeper issues.

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

This latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added new pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

#4155. Stalker 2’s first expansion officially revealed, and it's taking us to the power plant where it all began

Stalker 2’s first add-on isn’t far off, and it may just be the thing to bring you back to post-apocalyptic Chornobyl in 2026.

One of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the new Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Cost of Hope is the big news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

The story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two new regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two new regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

#4154. The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Updated (Version 1.1.1), Here Are The Patch Notes

Update [Wed 4th Nov 2026, 12:45pm]: The official patch notes have now gone live for Version 1.1.1 of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on the Switch 2.

It adds support for the Switch mobile app Zelda Notes and also fixes several issues to improve the overall game experience. Here's the rundown courtesy of Nintendo's Japanese support page:

After updating the software, please follow the instructions displayed at the start of the game to set up "ZELDA NOTES."

As Nintendo has previously explained, Zelda Notes allows you to see a record of your accomplishments, test your knowledge of the game, create and share your own ocarina melodies, and more. You don't need a Switch Online membership to use it, either.

You can find out the file size of this update and other information in the original story below:

Original Story: Some parts of the world are now just hours away from the launch of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2, and ahead of this, Nintendo has rolled out a new game update.

The anticipated release has been bumped from Version 1.0.0 to Version 1.1.1. Next time you check your game, you should be prompted to update. We had a look and can confirm our copy is also running on Version 1.1.1.

Based on the "manage software" section in the Switch 2 option menu, the remake is now 24.8GB in size, and this latest update is around 343MB to install. There are no patch notes just yet, but when we get an update about what's included, we'll let you know.

"Day one" and pre-release updates like this are pretty standard for Nintendo games nowadays, with the company often rolling them out to activate certain online features such as multiplayer. Star Fox also got a day one update when it returned earlier this year. Apart from overhauled graphics and gameplay updates, this latest remake includes support for amiibo and the Switch app Zelda Notes.

Again, if we hear any updates about this latest patch, we'll let you know. Have you been prompted to update your copy of Ocarina of Time yet? Have you got it digitally downloaded and ready to go, or are you picking up a physical copy? Let us know in the comments.

#4153. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Nationalise BioWare, basically. Well, sort of. "The developers at BioWare know how to run the studio," is what Avi Lewis, leader of Canada's New Democratic Party, wrote in a post following the closure. "They know how to make the games we all love. They should be given the first opportunity - and the federal support - to buy it and run it themselves. And if we want to avoid the Mass Effect effect in Canada, we should be keeping private equity out, not welcoming it in."

You can almost hear the horde of suit-wearing money-knowers who've sensed that suggestion's been made and are about to descend from orbit to yell about taxpayers' money being used to help ensure the creation of future adventures starring space blokes who say 'We'll bang, ok?'. The developers at BioWare know how to run the studio. They know how to make the games we all love. They should be given the first opportunity - and the federal support - to buy it and run it themselves.

In all seriousness, I'm not totally sure it'd work out in the long run, but it's something. An alternative to a company erasing a studio from existence because the Saudi Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner have been allowed to load them up with a ton of debt rather than reaching further into their own pockets.

Just make sure it's not some right-wing crank, or BioWare might run into some of the same problems it'd been feared their generally very inclusive games might face under Saudi ownership.

Rockstar Games has today shared more details on the launch of GTA 6, across both its digital and physical versions on PS5.

Rumoured last week via a social media account, it has now been confirmed that GTA 6 requires 212GB of space to be downloaded and installed. You'll be able to preload the game, and that option has actually been brought forward by two days.

GTA 6 preload will now be available from Tuesday, 10th November 2026. The title then releases for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on 19th November 2026.

Alternatively, there'll be a digital download of the GTA 6 boxart and the Leonida map, which I suppose you could just print out yourself.

#4149. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

#4148. Future? No Thanks! dev removes AI-generated voices from game and offers refunds to players who feel "betrayed"

Next game will be"completely hand-coded".

Open world ecosatire Future? No Thanks! has been updated to remove some AI-generated voices, after lead developer Paolo "Molleindustria" Pedercini belatedly disclosed his usage of the technology earlier this week. He's also offering to refund people over Paypal or Venmo if they "still feel betrayed" by this.

The update removes two instances of text-to-speech generated voicework for in-game robot characters – an automated toilet and an automated translator in a hair salon. In his previous blog, Pedercini wrote that he used genAI for these characters as a spoof of generative AI. He's decided to replace them with human voice-acting following a number of angry reactions on social media and some coverage in the press.

"The voices were recorded earlier this year but I decided to not use them because I thought the actual uncanny text-to-speech was funnier in that context," Pedercini writes in a new blog post. "Alas, the new generation of text-to-speech counts as user-facing AI-generated content and that keeps creating all sorts of annoyances and bad optics."

Pedercini still thinks the text-to-speech voices belong in Future? No Thanks! "In my opinion the game is worse now, but only, like, 0.001% worse," he observes. In less acrimonious tidings, he's also tweaked the game so that the "various gigs give you a bit more money, possibly preventing some situations of soft-locking players from achieving all the quests."

The blog includes a "personal update" in which Pedercini expounds rather bitterly upon the backlash to the game's genAI elements. "Somebody from Bluesky (the Twitter/X clone) dragged me due to a post disclosing what I foolishly thought a minor use of generative-AI in Future? No Thanks!" he writes. "I gave versions of that statement multiple times before, whenever asked by festivals and events. Steam doesn’t require disclosure of generative AI for things like code assistance so many people assume their favorite indie games don’t use AI at all just because the developers stay mum."

For context, Valve updated Steam's rules in January to allow "efficiency" tools, such as coding assistants. I'm basing this on anecdotes and conversations with other devs, rather than any kind of statistical survey, but it seems very likely that a lot of developers on Steam aren't disclosing their genAI use - the policy has always been more of a gesture on Valve's part than a mechanism of real accountability.

"Not me, I’m a good boy and I wanted a page I could link to that explains that NO, this is not a vibecoded slop game but YES, I did ask chatGPT to fix a broken shader and a few things like that," Pedercini goes on. "More foolishly, I added a paragraph that sounded like I was trying to exculpate myself by poo-pooing on all the colleagues that advocate for an AI-free life." (The paragraph in collection was deleted after the original blog's publication, but not before it had been screengrabbed and shared on the socials.)

"Look, it was not a good post," Pedercini concedes. "Defeatist, hastily written. I thought nobody would read it. Anyway, slow news day, everybody fucking hates AI, the whole scene piled on."

Pedercini proceeds to caricature some of the people yelling at him over social media: "Am I satirizing the puppy killing machine by KILLING PUPPIES?" He compares the anger he's received to being harrassed by Adam Baldwin's followers at the height of the Gamergate hate campaign.

Pedercini ends by sharing a list of developers who've sworn off generative AI. "Big props to them," he writes. "Give them a follow. SteamFest is drowning in actual slop, help them stand out. And I hate to break it to you, but you should probably assume that all the studios that have not made a public statement against all generative AI are using it for coding in some capacity. I’m guessing this episode isn’t going to encourage more voluntary disclosures." As for his next game, it'll be "completely hand-coded".

#4147. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4145. Factorio's final major update has rolled off the assembly line, adding "the things we wanted to do for 2.0 but didn't have time for"

Including QoL tweaks, new visuals, and more predictable asteroids

In one of the happier endings to occur in games this week, impossibly enormous resource management sim Factorio has just released its last-ever major update – version 2.1 – on its stable branch. As previously heads-upped by developers Wube Software, 2.1 doesn’t make any big new additions to its planets or tech trees, but does sneak in more than 30 quality of life improvements and minor new features for both the base game and its Space Age expansion. Including, they say, "the things we wanted to do for 2.0 but didn't have time for." Nice to get a few final pieces out the door before it closes, eh.

There’s also an updated trailer, if you want to watch promotional footage for a game that may well have enveloped your every waking moment since 2016.

Factorio - Trailer 2026 Watch on YouTube

Here are some of those changes I’ve picked out at random. "Mixed rockets: Rockets can now carry multiple different items in one launch, so no more sending a full stack of everything just to build a small platform." Nice! "Land mines can be used as tripwires and enemy detectors." Devious! "Asteroid damage now depends on the asteroid's remaining health instead of its speed, so it is much more predictable." Convenient! Not counting how you’re still being hit by an asteroid. There’s also now the ability to play Space Age without the controversial Quality mechanic, as well as the ability to flip pumpjacks and burner miners instead of merely rotating them, like some loser.

The 2.1 update also gives Factorio one last graphical polish, including a handful of new models and a "new pump rendering system that can connect to fluid wagons no matter how cursed your station is." I’m merely pretending to be a Factorio expert for the purposes of publishing this article, though I will say – from experience building piplines in Deep Rock Galactic – that a series of tubes is only truly cursed if it still works, in spite of itself, at transporting liquids. Otherwise you’ve just got a pile of broken pipes, again, like some loser.

This isn’t the end-end of Factorio, which Wube Software have said will continue to get bug fixes and support-level updates while they largely move on to "other game prototypes/experiments." Though even if it was, it’s had a bloomin' admirable run, starting with four years of early access - successful enough to cement it as the de facto basis for later automation-builders like Satisfactory and Dyson Sphere Program – and continuing to enrapture aspiring industrial managers into the present. Ollie has over 1,000 hours in it. Maybe I’m the loser for making light of it.

#4144. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

#4142. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4141. Skyrim's Successor Finally Re-Revealed as The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel

It's official: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is the full title of Bethesda's next open world RPG.

The subtitle has been announced as part of the developer's 40th anniversary celebrations. Confirmation comes via a very brief trailer at the end of the company's new video, which you can watch below.

The teaser shows sand blowing across an Elder Scroll, and it concludes with an ominous quote from Yazar, a Moth Priest (remember them from Oblivion?) in service of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

It reads: "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Obviously not, but the teaser and subtitle reveal nail down at least one thing: this game's going to take place in Sentinel, which is both a capital city and kingdom within Hammerfell — the home of the Redguards.

You can expect deserts, ancient ruins, and an adventure-filled coastline.

When we'll actually get to see The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is anyone's guess at this point. Bethesda has just warned that "it’ll be some time before we’re ready to share more". The wait continues...

#4140. Mass Effect 3 ending discourse ignored the RPG's scale, ambition, and exuberance, including that of its oddly great co-op

Ah, come on, it was fine. Better than fine. We can argue for another fourteen years about whether BioWare should have redone the ending or not, but Mass Effect 3 was really a compendium of endings, a ludicrously ambitious wrapping-up of dozens of plot threads, character arcs, and running gags. Even if you can point to other RPGs that, on an individual basis, are more branching and reactive, Mass Effect 3's largely successful closing of a galaxy's worth of choose-your-own adventure books - filled in and followed across three evolving instalments - showed an audacity and grandiosity that no other three-part series had matched before. Or, at least on that scale, has pulled off since.

Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives.

It didn't hurt that Mass Effect 3 also had the trilogy's fiercest, bangiest action by far, nor some of its highest-stakes, often most lip-chewing moments of decisionmaking. It is true that the accumulation of War Assets wasn't always as heavy on character drama as the game-long preparation for Mass Effect 2's Suicide Mission, but then you don't simply play Mass Effect 3 to make a number go higher. You play it to punch or hug reporters, to love or shoot your friends, to save or damn entire species. And it has loads of that, right up to the point to have to choose the colour of an explosion. Potentially beyond, if you treat the (assuredly, delightfully) fanservice-forward Citadel expansion as Shepard's true last ride.

Back in 2013, and again with 2021's Legendary Edition, I was sad that Mass Effect 3 ended and glad that it happened. That, at the risk of appearing less furious at EA's stewardship than I am, does not change with BioWare's closure. What does bother me is the uncertainty over what now happens to Mass Effect 3's surprisingly entertaining, weirdly long-lived co-op mode.

I don't doubt this was put in for boring, C-suite, "gamers want multiplayer" reasons. But that only gave the resultant palled-up superpower maelstroms a sense that they were better than they had any right to be, with explosive moments of player-to-player power synergies and spacious, blindspot-filled maps that could maintain a thrilling feeling of being permanently surrounded. Post-release additions to the species-spanning character roster also showed glimpses of that same, fuck-it swagger that BioWare exhibited in the campaign, as they increasingly moved away from familiar soldier archtypes towards electric whip wielders, regenerating lizards, teleporting ninjas, and three-foot-tall psychic asthmatics. While many of today's co-op shooters fret over miniscule balance changes, in pursuit of some mythically perfect meta, Mass Effect 3's gave you a crate of action figures and told you to go nuts.

While I haven't played it recently, there's a small but loyal contingent who do, and for their sake I hope the multiplayer's P2P setup helps it survive the EA cull. I was, and for now technically still is, too good to be doomed to oblivion. Or, worse, vibe-coded Legendary Edition mods.

#4139. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Is Reportedly Still "More Than Two Years Away"

After initially announcing The Elder Scrolls 6 all the way back in 2018, Bethesda has now officially confirmed its subtitle: Sentinel. Ooh.

However, if you're under the impression that this means the game is somewhat imminent, a new post from Bloomberg's Jason Schreier suggests that it is still "more than two years away" (thanks, Push Square).

I think a lot of people forget that The Elder Scrolls VI was only announced in 2018 (along with Starfield) to soften the blow of Fallout 76 — "Don't worry, even though we're making a multiplayer game we've got single-player stuff coming too!" Sorry to say this game is still more than 2 years away!

This, of course, would likely mean that its eventual release will land at least a decade following the game's announcement at E3 2018, which is frankly just ridiculous. And we thought the eight-year wait for Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was overkill.

It's just yet another indication that studios need to exercise some restraint when it comes to early announcements. As Schreier stated in his post, Bethesda seemingly wanted to balance out its Fallout 76 announcement with the promise of another single player-focused Elder Scrolls game, but we're not convinced anybody could have predicted what a long wait it would turn out to be.

Nintendo is pretty good at keeping its announcements under lock and key until the right moment these days, and we suspect that Prime 4 proved a big lesson for the company in this regard. Hell, Zelda: Ocarina of Time was only properly announced in June this year, and it's launching tomorrow at the time of writing. Can't argue with that!

#4138. I've got egg on my face because Steam's Personal Calendar feature has apparently been a test this whole time and is only now actually a fully fledged component

I'll be honest folks: I didn't know that Steam's Personal Calendar feature was still technically in testing. I've been using it here and there to keep track of what's come out recently or what's coming out imminently, and have generally found it to be fairly reflective of the kinds of games I was interested in. It just worked! Yet lo and behold, a post from Valve went out yesterday announcing that the feature has launched out of Steam Labs "and is considered a full feature of the Steam Store."

The feature, if you've missed it, is "another way to see recommended games for you, showing both recently released and upcoming games filtered down to the set of games we think you are most likely to be interested in," as Valve explain it anyway. "It uses your recently played games to find people with similar playtime profiles to you, and then looks at the games those players have been adding to their wishlist or playing." I do wonder if there's a bit more going under the hood here, as my playtime count is all over the place, with nothing above 50 hours on there, and that's an exception to the norm (I'm from more of a console background, alright).

But even still, my recommendations do remain pretty good, showing me games that I have since added to my wishlist. I'm never opposed to new discovery tools, especially considering how bad Valve can actually be at that kind of thing. Apparently the recommendation system refreshes daily "to incorporate the latest data. In reality you aren't likely to see your recommendations change all that much from day to day, but as time goes by you will obviously see new things pop up as the 8-week horizon of the calendar marches forward, or as games lock in their release dates."

This comes as part of a broader swathe of changes Valve have been introducing to Steam over the past couple of years, including one from last month that will change its homepage discounts and events section to be a bit more algorithm based. Perhaps it's some kind of weird prepwork for that new Half-Life they're almost definitely making but only talk about accidentally.

#4137. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4136. Paralives' first major update slips to next year, but when it comes you can expect some pretty meaty improvements for all of its main features

Since launch back in May of this year, life sim Paralives appears to have been trucking along nicely, with the dev team offering up fairly regular updates with all sorts of tweaks big and small. Certainly confidence-inspiring for an early access game, especially one as systems-driven as it is. And now, the Paralives team have outlined their plans for the game's first major update, which seem very catered to improving the core experience.

As part of a four point plan they outlined, first up on the docket is "buffing up the basics." This is all about strengthening some of the currently existing Live Mode systems. That means improvements to how relationships function by unlocking more things when a relationship level goes up, adding in more interactions that change your Para's emotions, improving the Community Centre's bundles and tweaking the economy curve so it isn't as easy to get money.

The next point is on expanding the Live Mode, meaning the addition of a pair of new skills, adding in more together and story cards, new relationship label unlockables, and more jobs too. Build Mode will also see some improvements, with a big focus on build breaking bugs. You can also expect new bits of furniture and items, and a tweak to furniture and item efficiency.

Lastly, there are also planned improvements to the Paramaker. One is by adding in more hairstyles and clothing items, notably baggy outfits, and the other is increasing the range of fat and muscle sliders "to represent a wider variety of body shapes." As a bigger person myself I'm always enthused when character creators actually let you have a fat body, so this is a welcome point from the dev team.

Worth noting that this list "is not final," and some things may be pushed back with others getting added in. Also worth noting is that while this first major update was planned for the end of 2026, it's been pushed into next year as the team needs a bit more time. You can read about all of these plans in more detail over on Steam.

#4135. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

Admittedly there's a chance you've not heard of it, that be the way of things in this algorithmically dominated world, but allow me to tell you about its big, scary world and the strange camera you're equipped with to capture all the sights it holds.

In the world of HELENA : Cloud District, you have come across a rotting megastructure that appears to be long abandoned, all sorts of strange flora dotted throughout it. In one part, it's something of a precision first-person platformer, as you navigate its intricately layered world with drops so steep you'd probably die before you hit the bottom. At the centre of it all is a computer, and it's here where you must bring all of your photographs in order to learn more about the history of the place.

The in-game camera itself is a fascinating thing to look at, completely impossible, alien and ancient in its design. From what I can tell it's a sort of metallic helmet, these insect-like segments snapping into place when you're gearing up to take a snap. You only appear to have three photo slots at any given point in time, meaning you can't just go gallivanting around the place all trigger happy like. There's an amount of care you have to put in positioning yourself and subsequently finding your way back to the central computer.

It's non-linear too, there's no set path you have to take, and it seems like there's some neat movement mechanics too. "Slide, hover, and glide through the structure in your own creative way in order to reach every level and get deeper into the slumbering Cloud District," explains the game's Steam page. Sounds like you don't have to worry too much about that falling to your death thing, then. I'm quite enthused by what HELENA : Cloud District is putting down, and it has a release date now too: October 29th. Same day as Hypnos! I now dub October 29th megastructure day. There will not be a vote on this matter. Ahead of HELENA's release, make sure to give it a wishlist on Steam.

#4133. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4132. South Of Midnight Director Reflects On Why He Was 'Always Worried' About Funding At Xbox

"It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable."

We absolutely loved South of Midnight when it launched last year as an Xbox first-party title from Compulsion Games, and it's still one of our favourite Xbox Game Studios releases of recent years. However, a year later, Xbox has parted ways with the development team and helped transition them back to an independent studio.

In a nutshell, it seems Xbox wasn't happy enough with South of Midnight's performance from a revenue standpoint, and the same could be said for other smaller releases last year like Double Fine's Keeper and Kiln.

Some fans had been voicing their concerns prior to these releases that Xbox might be putting too much funding into them, and speaking on a recent podcast, South of Midnight director David Sears admitted that he was "always worried" that the funding situation might change and cause Xbox to "close the floodgates".

Here's an excerpt from the MinnMax podcast in which he said this:

"I mean, [Xbox] were funding a lot of games. They were also funding a lot of studios that, you know, I was like, well, okay, great. I guess you have infinite money. Like I was saying earlier, I don't want to feel the weight of the obligation of giant budget or an army of 600 to be responsible for. I want to make something that isn't going to bankrupt Microsoft, I guess, or the games division."

"So, you know, on one hand, if everyone you're working with is either trying to make generational games at not a huge expense, or games that have huge or really significant contemporary commercial appeal, great. It's going to work. But when does that ever happen?"

"I literally told people, 'Wow, this could be terrible.' Because somebody is going to say one day, 'We're closing those floodgates.' And that's going to have really traumatic results downstream."

Perhaps most shockingly, the director went on to admit that as much as he wanted to make South of Midnight, it perhaps wasn't sustainable from a funding perspective in hindsight, and that a "shocking outcome" seemed inevitable.

"I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt, and obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, 'cause I'm not completely selfless. But it just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course it was going to have a shocking outcome."

"I mean, it's easy to dissect it now. At the time, I would talk to other directors and would be like, 'How is this happening? How did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now, right? There's always a night when Rome burns.' And I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Of course, none of this is to suggest that Sears wasn't proud of South of Midnight, or that he didn't think it was worthwhile, but it just appears he was concerned with the Xbox money was putting into (and expecting back) for it.

Nevertheless, it seems like he had a very positive experience working with Microsoft overall:

"To their credit, it's amazing, right? I think there's definitely corporate Microsoft DNA but they're vastly different from the Microsoft I knew back in the '90s or the early 2000s, right? Much more humane, actually. It's remarkable and commendable."

"Working on South of Midnight, it became clear to me - some games, their time is not on release. Some games are generational, right? Something that has a good message or is transportive to places that will remain timeless will endure and audiences will find them."

His prediction did ultimately come true - Xbox decided to "close the floodgates" earlier this year by splitting from multiple studios including Compulsion Games, and seemingly adopting a new strategy of focusing on their core franchises like Halo, Forza, Gears, Fallout and others.

We're just pleased that Compulsion Games didn't end up getting closed altogether, and that South of Midnight did actually see the light of day instead of being cancelled during development. We reckon it could end up being one of those Sunset Overdrive-style titles in the future - a cult classic that people end up really enjoying from years past.

#4131. South of Midnight's Director Wouldn't Have Funded It, Says Xbox's Approach Was Unsustainable

South of Midnight is the latest title from Compulsion Games, a studio that used to be under Microsoft's umbrella before it reclaimed its independence earlier this year.

It seemingly underperformed, even with ports to other platforms, including PS5, just under a year after its Xbox launch.

Now, in a new interview with Minnmax, the game's director, David Sears, has made new comments about the game and Xbox's funding at the time.

To summarise, he says that, while it was highly commendable of the company to support smaller, higher-risk titles such as South of Midnight and Double Fine's Keeper, it was ultimately unsustainable because the "infinite money" had to stop at some point.

"They were funding a lot of games," Sears says. "They were also funding a lot of studios that, you know, I was like 'well, okay, great, I guess you have infinite money, you do you, I want less. I don't want to feel the weight of the obligation of a giant budget, or an army of 600 to be responsible for. I want to make something that isn't going to bankrupt Microsoft or the games division.'"

"So on one hand, if everyone you're working with is either trying to make generational games at not a huge expense, or games that have huge or really significant contemporary commercial appeal – great, it's going to work. But when does that ever happen, right?"

Sears was "always worried" about South of Midnight suddenly losing funding, suggesting that if he was heading up Xbox, he "probably" would have done exactly that.

"I literally told people, 'Wow, this could be terrible.' Because somebody is going to say one day, 'We're closing those floodgates.' And that's going to have really traumatic results downstream."

"I mean, I wanted to make it, no doubt, right? Obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else’s money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, because I’m not completely selfless.

"But, you know, it just seems like in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable, so of course, it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome."

While there have been no official sales figures for South of Midnight, analytical estimates from Alinea back in April 2026 had the PS5 version specifically at about 16,000 sales.

Other data, such as Steam player counts, don't paint a particularly rosy picture either, and Sears' own comments in this interview also suggest it didn't hit its mark.

For a while, Xbox was funding games of all shapes and sizes in order to fill out Game Pass, but this approach, spearheaded by former CEO Phil Spencer, doesn't seem to be in place anymore, with his replacement, Asha Sharma, making severe cuts to get the business back on track.

South of Midnight is a great game, by the way, but if even the director was doubting its commercial potential, it was clearly not going to be a big seller.
